judged_text: TopicEmbed.import stores third-party HTML (RSS item content passed through CGI.unescapeHTML, or article HTML fetched from the embed URL) as post content with cook_method raw_html, which makes Post#cook return the raw string and skips the sanitizing rendering pipeline entirely; embed/best.html.erb then renders post.cooked with `raw`. A malicious or compromised feed or article yields stored JavaScript execution on the Discourse origin — in the embed iframe and on regular topic pages that render cooked — enabling session theft and moderator actions on behalf of visitors. CGI.unescapeHTML actively converts entity-encoded markup back into live tags, and the footer interpolates the unescaped #{url} into an HTML attribute, so even a well-behaved feed's link field is an injection vector. The new spec cements the invariant drop by asserting post.cooked == post.raw.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a `:raw_html` cook method (Post.cook_methods) and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitizing pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `embed/best.html.erb` renders `post.cooked` via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Feed importing also does `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` before storing content, which can turn entity-encoded markup into live tags. Additionally, `TopicEmbed.import` interpolates the unescaped `url` into an HTML `<a href='#{url}'>` string (only guarded by a loose `^https?://` regex), making attribute injection plausible. The accompanying spec asserts `post.cooked == post.raw`, cementing the unsanitized behavior. This is a verifiable stored XSS/security defect introduced by the diff.
